summary: The note presents interviews with spokespeople from six local political parties about their approaches to public health. Strategies range from environmental regulation and preventive care to digital health, mental health funding, community-led assessments, economic measures, and opioid crisis response. It concludes that local parties act as stewards of communal well-being and can serve as testing grounds for wider health policy.
one_line: Interviews with six local political parties reveal diverse public health strategies, from environmental and tech-driven approaches to mental health, community involvement, economics, and opioids.
key_facts: Adam Peters, health policy chair of the Green Roots Party, was interviewed on October 15, 2023; the party campaigns for stricter environmental regulations and more urban parks.
The Green Roots Party believes preventive measures will reduce health care spending by limiting chronic diseases.

Sylvia Moreno, local chair of the Techno-Democratic Party, was interviewed on September 20, 2023; the party backs telehealth, health monitoring apps, and more funding for digital health infrastructure.
The Techno-Democratic Party is campaigning for better broadband in rural areas to support health technologies.
Dr. Evan Campbell, spokesperson for the New Harmony Party, was interviewed on November 3, 2023; the party wants mental health treated on par with physical health.

The New Harmony Party plans to increase mental health funding and add mental health education in schools, paid for by reallocating existing health funds and raising taxes on alcohol and tobacco sales.

Layla Quinn, spokesperson for the Civic Engagement Coalition (CEC), was interviewed on December 1, 2023; the CEC favors a bottom-up approach with community-led health assessments and local health committees.
Rajiv Mehta, economic strategist for the Prosperity for All Party, was interviewed on October 29, 2023; the party aims to improve health through job creation and small business support.
The Prosperity for All Party's policies aim to eliminate food deserts, increase the minimum wage, and ensure affordable healthcare services.
Kendra Watkins, health campaign manager for the United Community Front, was interviewed on September 25, 2023, about the opioid epidemic.

The United Community Front calls for more stringent prescription monitoring programs and greater investment in treatment facilities, along with education and awareness campaigns and accessible recovery services.
